To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have spatially resolved a massive protostellar core with a mass of 0.29 {+-} 0.04 M{sub Sun } at an early evolutionary stage, which is one of the best examples of an intermediate-mass protocluster core, and have found that the core is composed of a large number of substructures with a mass of about 0.07 M{sub Sun }.

we have discovered an extremely young intermediate-mass protocluster, MMS 5/6/OMC3, in the Orion Molecular cloud-2/3 (OMC2/3) region, and that the sub-clump structures are distributed in the envelope of the MMS6-main peak.
we have spatially resolved a massive envelope of an intermediate-mass protobinary system at the very early stage of star formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and dynamics of the molecular cloud complex associated with the star forming region W3(OH).
the study of the physical properties and the dynamical evolution of the circumstellar disks around young stars in star-forming regions in the Milky Way.
the study of the structure and dynamics of the interstellar medium (ISM), and its relation to star formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observations of the Orion Molecular Clouds 1-3 are consistent with the idea that the star-forming gas is clumpy.
the observed properties of MMS 1-4 are not in contradiction with the predictions of the theory of core formation, evolution, and collapse.
the observational data of MMS 1-6 are not consistent with the predictions of the standard model of low-mass star formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have spatially resolved the substructures in the envelope around the intermediate-mass prototypical protostar MMS 6.
we have spatially resolved a protostellar core with a disk-like structure, which is one of the earliest stages for intermediate-mass stars, for the first time.
the substructures within the massive envelope of MMS 7 are not yet understood, and the origin of these substructures is still an open question.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the submillimeter continuum emission of MMS 1-3 can be modeled as a single protostellar core with a disk-like structure.
MMS 3/OMC-2 is one of the best examples of an early stage of massive star formation.
MMS 1 is a very massive, dense, and young protostellar core.
